structure: Part 1 read in full e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js (440 lines, 22 tests in 5 describes), e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (48 lines). The spec opens with three copy tables (REASON_HINTS, INTERNAL_MARKET_PURPOSES, and later GERMINAL_REASON_HINTS, GERMINAL_PURPOSE_HINTS, GERMINAL_SEMEN_RESULTS) and then walks section 1 of the task list in journey order: 'notification type' (3 tests: /create-notification redirect to /notification-type with its five options, Continue-with-nothing error and live animals to origin with a GBN-AG draft reference; category dashboard Create new skipping the question; plants for planting reaching an empty commodity search), 'origin of the import' (4 tests: page copy and buttons; region-code Yes reveal, empty-code error and country prefix; country optional with answers kept; country autocomplete), 'what are you importing' (5 tests: page copy, buttons, cancel and help details; nothing-selected error; cattle search results and selection panel; several commodities and Clear all; save and return to overview without validating), 'main import reason' (7 tests: five reasons with hints; reason optional; internal market purposes and error; transhipment destination country; transit port of exit and destination country; temporary admission horses exit date, real-date error and port of exit; the /prototype/reason-for-import seed route) and 'germinal products: section 1' (3 tests: germinal dashboard Create new to origin with the germinal status strip; germinal commodity search for semen and embryos with selection; germinal reasons and purposes with their hints, errors and onward route to /consignment-details). journey.js gives the /design-release-2.1 mount, the error-summary, inline-error, back-link and draft-reference assertions, the action-button values, the autocomplete, commodity-search and date-picker helpers, the SPECIES fixtures and the startNotification, answerOrigin, answerCommodity and answerReason steps; only what these tests call is claimed here. fixtures.js only records each test's visited pages for the trace index, so it yields no product claim. The part stops at /consignment-details, which part 2 covers.
